statewide.fact: Discover Pass required to park at Washington State Parks, DNR and WDFW lands (including water access areas) unless the vehicle displays a WDFW Vehicle Access Pass (WDFW lands only). VAP is free with an annual hunting, trapping or fishing license (not razor clam/shellfish) and transfers between 2 vehicles. Prices with processing fees: $51.50/yr, $11.50/day.
'A Discover Pass or Vehicle Access Pass is required at all WDFW recreation lands.' Some WDFW-owned sites are managed by other agencies under those agencies' rules.
Discover Pass $45/yr or $10/day before fees; $99 citation for not displaying; not needed when arriving by boat or non-motorized means, but vehicles towing boat trailers must display it.
2026 Discover Pass free days: Jan 1, Jan 19, Mar 9, Mar 19, Apr 22, Jun 6-7, Jun 19, Aug 9, Sep 26, Oct 10, Nov 11.
Washington State Parks watercraft launch fee: $7/day (at State Parks launches).

WDFW Aquatic Invasive Species prevention permit ($24) applies to boats not registered in Washington, seaplanes and commercial transporters; canoes, kayaks and other unregistered small craft are exempt.
Olympic National Park: all visitors need an entrance pass ($30 private vehicle, 7 days; $15 per person on foot/bike; cashless).

averill-pateros.text: Discover Pass or WDFW Vehicle Access Pass at Averill (WDFW); Pateros take-out is Douglas PUD.

big-eddy-sultan.text: Big Eddy is a State Parks-managed access (per WDFW): Discover Pass required. Sultan take-out fee status not confirmed.

big-eddy-twisp.outstanding: No managing-agency page found for Big Eddy (Methow) or the Twisp take-out.

big-horn-umtanum.text: BLM charges a $5 day-use fee ($15 overnight) at its Yakima River Canyon recreation sites, which are open year-round (https://www.blm.gov/visit/yakima-river-canyon-campgrounds).

bridge-view-concrete-bridge.text: King County lists a public hand-boat access just below the Concrete Bridge with road-shoulder parking; no pass is stated. Bridge View fee status not confirmed.
bridge-view-concrete-bridge.outstanding: Bridge View manager/fee not found (likely USFS road corridor; unconfirmed).

bz-husum.text: USFS: no fees at BZ Corner or the Husum Boating Site for private boaters; commercial outfitters need a USFS special-use permit.

carlton-averill.text: Discover Pass or WDFW Vehicle Access Pass required at both WDFW sites.

concrete-bridge-tanner.text: King County lists a public hand-boat access just below the Concrete Bridge with road-shoulder parking; no pass is stated. At Tanner use only the designated parking (AW).

copper-marblemount.text: No fee: NPS says there is no fee to raft the Skagit in a personal raft (Copper Creek), and USFS says no fees are required at Marblemount Boat Launch. USFS asks boaters to avoid beaching between Marblemount and Rockport bridges.

dryden-cashmere.text: Dryden is a WDFW access: Discover Pass or WDFW Vehicle Access Pass required. Cashmere Riverside Park fee status not confirmed.
dryden-cashmere.outstanding: City of Cashmere pages could not be read (blocked/empty); Riverside Park fee unknown. News reports say the ramp was blocked by flood rock in spring 2026 with repairs targeted by Apr 30, 2026 (not confirmed complete).

flaming-geyser-whitney.text: Flaming Geyser State Park requires a Discover Pass. No fee or hours found for King County's Whitney Bridge Park.

goodell-copper.text: No fee: NPS says there is no fee to raft the Skagit in a personal raft (https://www.nps.gov/thingstodo/rafting-in-the-north-cascades.htm).

headworks-kanaskat.text: Discover Pass required at Kanaskat-Palmer State Park.

hoh-campground-oxbow.text: Put-in is inside Olympic National Park: entrance pass required ($30 per private vehicle, 7 days; cashless). Oxbow take-out manager and pass not confirmed.
hoh-campground-oxbow.outstanding: Oxbow take-out manager (DNR assumed in v1) not confirmed.

icehouse-turkey-hole.text: Both ends are WDFW water-access sites: Discover Pass or WDFW Vehicle Access Pass required. Turkey Hole is take-out only (WDFW).

kanaskat-flaming-geyser.text: Discover Pass required at both Kanaskat-Palmer and Flaming Geyser state parks.

lake-wenatchee-plain.text: Lake Wenatchee State Park: Discover Pass required plus a $7/day Watercraft Launch Fee; launch hours summer 6:30 a.m.-dusk, winter 8 a.m.-dusk (parks.wa.gov). Plain take-out fee status not confirmed.

leavenworth-peshastin.text: Discover Pass required at Peshastin (WDFW). Leavenworth Waterfront Park is free (AW).

leidl-icehouse.text: Both ends are WDFW water-access sites: Discover Pass or WDFW Vehicle Access Pass required.

lmuma-roza.text: BLM charges a $5 day-use fee ($15 overnight) at its Yakima River Canyon recreation sites, which are open year-round (https://www.blm.gov/visit/yakima-river-canyon-campgrounds). Take out at Roza; Roza Dam is downstream.

lower-sauk-government-bridge.text: USFS says no fees are required at Lower Sauk Boat Launch (day use, sunrise to sunset). Government Bridge is an informal access; fee status not confirmed.
lower-sauk-government-bridge.outstanding: Government Bridge is informal; manager/fee not found.

marblemount-howard-miller.text: Howard Miller Steelhead Park (Skagit County) charges a small ramp-use fee (AW; amount not verified).

meenach-plese-flats.text: Discover Pass required at Riverside State Park (Plese Flats).

plain-hwy2.outstanding: No managing-agency page found for Plain Access or the Hwy 2 bridge take-out; fee/pass unknown.

plum-landing-fall-city.text: Discover Pass required at Plum Landing (WDFW).

queets-trailhead-streator.text: Olympic National Park requires an entrance pass for all visitors ($30 per private vehicle, valid 7 days; the park is cashless).

red-barn-big-eddy.outstanding: Red Barn is the Town of Winthrop's Mack Lloyd Park (WWRP grant record); no Town fee page found. Big Eddy (Methow) manager unknown.

salmon-hatchery-trout-hatchery.text: Both launches are run by Tacoma Power, which says there is no fee to use them (Blue Creek allows camping up to 3 days, no fires).

sauk-prairie-lower-sauk.text: USFS says no fees are required at Lower Sauk Boat Launch (day use, sunrise to sunset). Fee status at Sauk Prairie not confirmed.

streator-hartzell.text: Olympic National Park requires an entrance pass for all visitors ($30 per private vehicle, 7 days); whether Hartzell Creek is inside the park boundary is not confirmed.
streator-hartzell.outstanding: Park boundary status of Hartzell Creek launch unconfirmed.

sultan-lewis-street.text: Discover Pass required at Lewis Street (WDFW).

troy-boggans.text: Oregon Waterway Access Permit required for non-motorized boats on the Oregon part of the river; since Jan 1, 2026 it applies to boats of any length ($6/7 days, $20/yr). WDFW Boggans take-out: Discover Pass or WDFW Vehicle Access Pass.

troy-heller-bar.text: Oregon Waterway Access Permit on the Oregon portion (all non-motorized boats as of 2026). Heller Bar is a WDFW water access area — Discover Pass or WDFW Vehicle Access Pass for parking.

umtanum-lmuma.text: BLM charges a $5 day-use fee ($15 overnight) at its Yakima River Canyon recreation sites, which are open year-round (https://www.blm.gov/visit/yakima-river-canyon-campgrounds).

vernita-white-bluffs.text: Discover Pass required to park at Vernita Bridge (WDFW-managed, per NPS). No camping at Vernita (WDFW).

conflicts: v1 point notes said Barrier Dam and Blue Creek require a Discover Pass/VAP (as WDFW sites); Tacoma Power, which manages both launches, says there is no fee. WDFW notes some sites are managed by other agencies under their rules. Section notes now use Tacoma Power's statement.
